quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Meets our preferred position: Vendor IP indemnity extending to affiliates (20.1), plus indemnities for breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2); standard procedure in 20.4; infringement remedies (procure/modify/replace/refund) in 20.5. Our reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow (unmodified Customer material and unlawful use) and indemnities sit outside the cap as Excluded Claims under 21.3.

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: Meets our preferred position: we retain all rights in Customer Data and our pre-existing IP (14.1), own Deliverables with an express Vendor assignment (14.2), Vendor keeps only Vendor Technology with the perpetual paid-up licence back under 13.2 (14.3), and no joint ownership arises absent a separate signed instrument (14.4). 15.1 also bars model training on our data without consent. Ownership is conditioned on payment of the applicable Fees, which we note but do not treat as a deviation.

quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Meets our preferred position: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages waiver (with helpful direct-damage clarifications), and Excluded Claims covering confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. 21.3 also confirms our payment obligation is not "damages" and is uncapped, and 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability.

quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Meets our preferred position: free affiliate/successor assignment for us (24.1), Vendor assignment (including by change of control) requires our consent and never to a competitor (24.2), and 24.4 bars any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing or fee acceleration on our change of control. 13.3 carries licence rights across a permitted assignment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation: our position is that we retain freedom to source from other suppliers, and this clause also contradicts Sections 2.1 and 12.3. If some protection is needed, we could accept exclusivity limited to a defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically if Vendor misses service levels or delivery dates.

quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
rationale: Full-term exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit is walk-away territory under our playbook, and it contradicts Sections 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment). We propose deleting it, with a defined-category, 12-month exclusivity ending on service-level failure available as a fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages payable by us for dependency delays; we do not accept penalties or liquidated damages against the Customer. Vendor's remedy for a genuine Customer-caused delay is relief from the affected schedule and time-and-materials charges for demonstrable standby costs.

quote: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
rationale: A USD 25,000 per day penalty on us, triggered by any dependency delay however minor and with no cap, fails our position that no liquidated damages are payable by Customer and is walk-away territory. We have deleted it; Vendor retains schedule relief and can recover demonstrable standby costs.

quote: Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
rationale: Meets our preferred position: the grant expressly covers Affiliates and contractors worldwide (13.1), delivered/paid-up material carries a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence (13.2), and revocation or suspension is limited to a material uncured breach after notice and cure, with transferability to an Affiliate or successor (13.3). The use restrictions in 13.4 are narrow and expressly preserve our use of Customer Data and output.

rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, buy, build and compete in any field or territory. The exclusivity in 2.2 and the MFN in 7.2 conflict with this section but are addressed under EXCLUSIVITY and MFN respectively rather than double-flagged here.

We can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience right as new 9.6

quote: Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable.
rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and Customer-specific cause triggers (9.1–9.3), plus a force-majeure exit in 27.3; there is no termination-for-convenience right for either party. Under a three-year term (8.1) the absence of a Customer convenience right is a deviation, so we have inserted a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and confirmed Vendor has none. Favourably, no Vendor convenience right exists.

We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, in business hours, through an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and removed system access; the cost allocation (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) in 22.2 already meets our preferred position.

rationale: Meets our preferred position: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, and no arbitration (foreign or otherwise). The pre-suit executive escalation in 28.3 expressly preserves urgent relief and limitations filings, so it is not an obstacle.

quote: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
rationale: This is an open-ended MFN running against us — an obligation to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier — which is walk-away territory and inconsistent with 12.3's disclaimer of most-favoured-customer commitments. We propose deletion; MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.

The exclusivity in 2.2 could operate as a de facto lock-in, but we address that under EXCLUSIVITY rather than flagging the same term twice.
